summary: Interpreted the corrected revision: all five comparisons hold, so the shutdown account no longer rests on event values with an ambiguous admission. The unbuffered Barrier and Apply answered all eight post-shutdown calls in every trial, VerifyLeader answered 4, 4 and 5 of eight (11 of 24 futures incomplete), and enabling BatchApplyCh — the option whose own comment says it buffers applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and breaks the Apply timeout guarantee — flipped the two unaffected kinds: Barrier answered 6, 3 and 4 of eight and Apply 3, 3 and 5, stranding 11 and 13 of 24. That is a causal rather than correlational demonstration, since only the channel's buffering differs between answered and stranded cases while the call shape, future type and absent shutdown channel are identical. I extended the existing Fact under its own id with the corrected figures and the config-flip evidence, re-bound the interpretation to the corrected experiment with its receipt cited, kept the racing form as the timing-dependent manifestation two later runs did not reproduce, and replaced the limitation about unresolved batched comparisons with accurate ones about buffer size, sample counts and the 500ms classification. No execution requested. Remaining: the buffer was never filled, so blocking sends were not exercised.
